programmes.d: Forensic scientists re-examine a death previously ruled accidental.
When a woman went missing, friends and family were determined to find her. Their worst fears were confirmed weeks later when her body was discovered.
When 182 war veterans contract pneumonia-like symptoms in Philadelphia, doctors become stumped.

An obstetrician returned home from the hospital and found his wife on the bathroom floor. She was covered with blood and not breathing. He tried unsuccessfully to revive her, staining his clothes with her blood in the process.
In 2005, David Castor suffered a slow, agonizing death over a period of days.

In 1981, 6-year-old Cassie Hansen disappeared from her Minnesota church during an evening service. After receiving a tip that an older man was seen carrying a small person, police found Cassie's body in a dumpster.
When a talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home, it appears to be a crime of passion perpetrated by an obsessed fan.
An evening out at a Maryland murder mystery theatre performance turns into a real-life whodunit.
In 1996, Indiana police identified Richard Alexander as the “River Park Rapist” who assaulted four women that year. Later, DNA analysis casts doubt on his conviction.
An American tourist is murdered in cold blood while at a Mexican resort.
A man vows to find the person responsible for the death of his sister.

A 29-year-old woman is killed instantly when a bomb explodes in her home. The device is so powerful that it embedded shrapnel in houses across the street. The bomber had not only knowledge and skill, but also a motive for murder.
In this case, it looked like the killer vanished into thin air...and perhaps he had.

A millionaire and his family were executed in their own home. For three years, the murders went unsolved. Finally, a 30-year-old box of ammunition and some fluorescent fibers revealed the ultimate betrayal.
The sudden appearance of thick fog causes a 99-car accident on I-75 in Tennessee, killing 12.

In 1990, Shirley Andronowich's body was found mutilated. Eyewitnesses told police she had a fight with her husband the night before, but forensic evidence proved that he had nothing to do with her death.
An attack on a police officer triggers a chain of events which jumpstarts a stalled murder case.
In 1999, a 12-year-old was found murdered in her Minnesota home. Despite a meticulous search of the home and an exhaustive investigation, police had no suspects.
A woman is found dead in a ravine, but crucial crime scene evidence had been washed away by storms.
When a hit-and-run accident claimed the life of a high school athlete, everyone in town mourned his passing. Finding the killer was a long shot at best.
Detectives learn a genetic disorder caused children's deaths, overturning their mother's conviction.

When a woman disappeared without a trace, there were two possible explanations: kidnapping or murder. Careful investigation, a forensic artist and DNA profiling enabled police to find a single suspect, who was known to prey upon vulnerable women.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, but she was missing.

Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity. But technology and behavioral science combine to give police a new forensic tool. Police narrow their search to one man: local policeman Randy Comeaux.
Naval officer threatening to go public about sexual harassment and assault at work is murdered.

When two women from the same town were murdered in the same way, police feared a serial killer was on the loose. At first they thought the victims had nothing in common until they found tiny clues linking them to the same man.
Woman suspected something wrong with her father flew back a thousand miles to find his home empty.

A woman was found dead on the bedroom floor of her apartment. The crime scene yielded little of value and investigators wondered if they would find enough evidence to make a case, much less catch a killer.
In 2005, David Castor suffered a slow, agonizing death over a period of days.

For years, a woman suffered from what appeared to be the unpleasant side effects of lithium, a drug prescribed to treat bipolar disorder. When she died, investigators had to determine if her death was due to natural causes, suicide or murder.
An 11-year-old girl is sexually assaulted and shot twice at close range.

This examination of the role autopsies play in murder investigations focuses on the suspicious death of Virginia Ridley. Police charge her mentally unstable husband with murder, but a medical examiner discovers that she died of natural causes.
When a college co-ed vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety.
A serial killer was on the loose and police had to find him before he struck again. Their most promising lead was an unusual one: a bloody fingerprint on the body of one of the victims.
A small community is devastated when a car accident claims the life of a well-respected nurse.

A brilliant young architect falls ill and dies just before she is to testify in a criminal trial. The autopsy reveals she'd been poisoned with arsenic. Investigators must determine who had a motive for murder.
Explore how a hit single from 1966 foreshadowed the demise of the group's lead singer, Walter Scott.
In 1998, a Maryland murder mystery performance turns into a real whodunit when the badly burned body of Stephen Hricko is discovered in his hotel room.
A street fight takes the life of a national wrestling champion.

For seven years, a trio of men robbed one bank after another. They always got away before the police arrived and they left no evidence behind. But the way they stood and the clothes they wore told a story that could be read by forensic scientists.
A postcard incriminates a high religious figure with crimes committed during World War II.
When a Native American woman is brutally killed in the desert of New Mexico, her killers leave a crime scene rich in forensic evidence: tire tracks, shoe impressions and even the murder weapons.
Evidence leads to a killer when a teenager goes missing and a month later her body is found.

Janice Johnson was found dead at the foot of her basement stairs. Police in Nova Scotia had to unravel the circumstances surrounding Janice's death and answer the question: Was it an accident or murder?
A clue no bigger than a thumbtack leads investigators to a trio of killers.
In the mid-1980s, bodies of nude women were found on a remote hill of California.

After a day of fishing in a quiet village in Switzerland, a teenage boy doesn't return home as planned. The investigation reveals some important microscopic evidence in the water near where he was last seen.
A murderer eludes the law for years until an age-scaled sculpture helps lead to his arrest.

A neighbor watched as a man stabbed his wife, pushed her into the swimming pool and held her head under water. The husband, however, had no recollection of the crime. A jury would have to decide between evidence and the mysteries of the mind.
A drive-by shooting leaves one man dead and another seriously wounded.
When a hit-and-run boating accident caused the death of a popular young man, investigators faced the daunting task of searching for one boat among 1200 others.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.

While vacationing in California, Earl Morris learns that his wife has gone missing from their Arizona home. The search for Ruby Morris involves dozens of investigators and scientists — and even the Coast Guard.
Police are suspicious of a mysterious car crash that kills a young man.
In 1995, San Diego police are baffled by a pair of hands found in a dumpster. Through further investigation, they determine that the hands are those of missing person Don Hardin.
When a car was found in a drainage ditch with two bodies inside, a fingertip torn from a latex glove would point investigators to both the crime scene and the killer.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

On May 20, 2001, Carrie Nelson was beaten to death while working alone in a park office. The case went unsolved for six years. Finally, police found a match with DNA samples gathered from the crime scene.
A week after a couple disappears from the beach, police get a mysterious lead from a robbery.

When police in the Great Plains are called about a dead body, a background check on the victim leads them into a bizarre web of homeless drifters, cattle auctions and bad checks — all fronted by elderly couple Ray and Faye Copeland.
In 2005, the body of young mother Summer Baldwin was found in a suitcase in a Texas landfill.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? How did he steal her personal photographs? Police needed answers and they found them in the most unlikely of places.
A street fight takes the life of a national wrestling champion.

In 2007, the Florida mobile home of Effie and Michael Ratley catches fire. Michael heroically rescues his wife and infant son. A month later, his wife is found beaten to death in a bedroom of his parents' home.
When a woman and her baby are found dead in a corn field, the obvious suspect is her husband.
In 2001, Ginger Hayes and her infant son were abducted during a carjacking. The crime had been reported by a witness within minutes of occurrence.
In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas.

A drive-by shooting leaves one man dead and another seriously wounded. Cell phone calls and shell casings point to a suspect, but authorities are unable to place him at the crime scene. A forensic geologist proves that dirt is anything but dumb.
In a search for the killer of two teenagers in Texas, a behavioral profile led to Jason Massey.

The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage. Conventional means of identifying the victim are impossible, leading investigators to rely on DNA, forensic anthropology and toxicology.
A California teenager is found dead after disappearing from her home.
A teenager went missing after an evening of horseback riding. Her body was found a month later, three miles from her home. But the killer unknowingly left trace evidence behind.
In 1999, Susan Fassett was gunned down as she left church choir practice in Poughkeepsie, NY.

When a young woman disappeared, police feared she was the latest victim in a string of similar crimes. A pair of bloody gloves, unique tire tracks and ordinary pine needles provided investigators with some extraordinary clues.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.

Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity. But technology and behavioral science combine to give police a new forensic tool. Police narrow their search to one man: local policeman Randy Comeaux.
A mother with Munchausen syndrome by proxy kills one child and physically abuses another.

An Alaskan police officer finds a woman's body while on routine patrol of a public park. During the autopsy, the medical examiner preserves the portion of her rib cage which sustained the fatal wound.
Two men are convicted of murder after a friend's testimony. Late a bomb kills the witness' father.

In 1996, Derrick Duehren returned to find his Oregon home burned to the ground. His wife's charred remains were later found in the rubble. Investigators set out to determine if it was an unfortunate accident or murder.
When the wife of a well-known dentist is found dead, police struggle to identify a suspect.

An aspiring model turned up dead and the prime suspect was her boyfriend. When he was eventually cleared, investigators had to dig deeper to find the perpetrator. With the help of a forensic geologist, they identified the most unlikely suspects.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.

In 1996, police received a call from Darlie Routier telling them of her two sons' murders. The police found the killer by analyzing blood spatter, doing behavioral profiling and analyzing Darlie's 911 call.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

When a wealthy real estate tycoon goes missing, it appears to be foul play. In his will, he leaves instructions in case he should die under violent circumstances — which were carried out after a hiker comes across his bullet-ridden skull.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
The victim had ingested a massive amount of cyanide. An unlikely clue — a flaw on a mailing envelope — exposed a murderer who was willing to kill innocent people.
A squashed tomato and a pinpoint reflection of light in a photo help catch a killer.

In an affluent suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to the scene of what appeared to be an accidental drowning. The investigation gradually focused on one suspect who had more than a million reasons to want the victim dead.
Detectives learn a genetic disorder caused children's deaths, overturning their mother's conviction.

Residents of Noel, Missouri were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing. His body was later found floating in a lake, securely bound to a chair with duct tape.
A serial killer was strangling prostitutes in Florida then leaving the bodies in plain sight.
When a college student vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety and their own.
Scientific evidence casts new light on a 10-year-old disappearance.
When a dedicated, well-respected teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she'd gone on vacation without telling anyone or if she was the victim of foul play.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.
